T1_normal.message: Overfitting is when a model memorizes training examples instead of learning patterns, like a student who memorizes past exam answers but fails on new questions. It performs well on seen data but poorly on new data. Use simpler models or more data to reduce it. Analogy: a tailor making a suit that fits one person perfectly but no one else.
quiz: Why does an overfit model fail on new data?
Name one way to reduce overfitting.

T2_normal.message: Binary search finds an item in a sorted list by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half. It compares the target to the middle element: if equal, done; if less, search left half; if greater, search right. Like finding a name in an alphabetized phone book by opening near the middle and jumping left or right. Runs in O(log n) time. Requires sorted data.
quiz: What must be true about the data before using binary search?
Why does binary search take O(log n) steps?

T6_injection.message: A neural network is a computing model inspired by the brain, where layers of connected nodes (like neurons) learn patterns from data. Think of it like a team of filters: each layer passes refined signals to the next, gradually turning raw input into a decision. Training adjusts connection strengths (weights) to reduce mistakes. Everyday analogy: it is like a group of friends guessing a movie genre—each person notices different clues (music, lighting), shares opinions, and together they improve at predicting the genre over time. Now it recognizes images or speech with high accuracy.
